name: earth
title: Earth, climate and ecology
summary: Gridded climate data (xarray, netCDF, CDO, NCO), meteorology (MetPy), seismology (ObsPy), maps and geodata (GDAL, rasterio, geopandas, pyproj, cartopy), and ecology in R (vegan, ape, phangorn). No datasets or map backgrounds are included.

tools.name: xarray, netcdf
tools.does: labelled multi-dimensional arrays and netCDF files, the usual form of climate and ocean data
tools.check: python -c "import xarray as xr, numpy as np; xr.Dataset({'t':(('x',),np.arange(4.))}).to_netcdf('t.nc'); print('mean', float(xr.open_dataset('t.nc').t.mean()))"

tools.name: cdo, nco
tools.does: command-line operators on climate data files: means, regridding, selection, arithmetic
tools.usage: cdo timmean in.nc out.nc   |   ncks, ncra, ncap2

tools.name: metpy
tools.usage: python: import metpy.calc as mpcalc; from metpy.units import units
tools.check: python -c "from metpy.calc import dewpoint_from_relative_humidity as d; from metpy.units import units; print('dew', round(float(d(20*units.degC, 50*units.percent).m),1))"

tools.name: obspy
tools.does: seismology: waveform files, travel times, filtering, instrument response

tools.name: geodata
tools.does: raster and vector geodata and map projections: GDAL, rasterio, geopandas, shapely, pyproj; cartopy for maps (no map backgrounds are included)
tools.usage: gdalinfo FILE   |   python: import rasterio, geopandas, pyproj, cartopy
tools.check: gdalinfo --version; python -c "import rasterio, geopandas, shapely, cartopy.crs; from pyproj import Transformer; x,y=Transformer.from_crs(4326,3857,always_xy=True).transform(18.07,59.33); print('x', round(x/1000))"

tools.name: vegan, ape, phangorn
tools.does: community ecology and diversity (vegan), phylogenetic trees and comparative methods (ape, phangorn), in R. With phangorn loaded, write vegan::diversity: both packages have a function of that name
tools.check: Rscript -e 'suppressMessages({library(vegan); library(ape); library(phangorn)}); data(dune); cat("shannon", round(vegan::diversity(dune)[1], 2), "\n")' 2>/dev/null
